title: Zigbee network becomes extremely slow after Home Assistant Core update
body: Since updating Home Assistant Core from 2022.9.0 to 2022.9.1, my ZHA network has become extremely slow. Turning a light on or off can take more than 30 seconds or fail entirely. I run Home Assistant OS with a zzh stick. The log shows zigpy-znp request timeouts and asyncio TimeoutError exceptions.

symptoms_visible: Since updating to Home Assistant Core 2022.9.1, turning a Zigbee light on or off can take more than 30 seconds or fail entirely.
The log contains zigpy-znp callback timeouts and asyncio TimeoutError exceptions.
N0.label: N0 severe ZHA delay reported

symptoms_visible: After downgrading to 2022.9.0, my Zigbee devices respond normally again.
N1.label: N1 downgrade restores responsiveness

symptoms_visible: After updating to 2022.9.2, my Zigbee network initially responds normally.
N2.label: N2 issue initially absent on later patch

symptoms_visible: The delay is intermittent, and after updating to 2022.9.4 it is back.
N3.label: N3 intermittent delay recurs

symptoms_visible: My Zigbee motion and door sensors update immediately, but commands sent to lights can be ignored or arrive one to five minutes later.
The same log period contains repeated errors saying that a NoneType object has no attribute request_callback_rsp.
N4.label: N4 directional failure and connection errors established

symptoms_visible: On one affected setup, disabling Bluetooth makes Zigbee work better but it is still slower than before.
On another affected setup, Bluetooth was already disabled while the Zigbee delays and interruptions continued.
N4_x.label: N4_x Bluetooth workaround incomplete

symptoms_visible: Two other affected users report that their Zigbee devices work without delay after updating to 2022.10.2.
I have not reported a final retest of that release on my own system.
N_terminal.label: terminal other users report recovery, reporter unverified

solution.intent: Temporarily downgrade to the last known-working Home Assistant Core release to restore Zigbee responsiveness and confirm the version correlation.
solution.concrete_example: Restore the previous Core release and check whether the same lights respond normally again.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1, c3 and c9: the original reporter independently downgraded from 2022.9.1 to 2022.9.0 and observed normal operation. This is a temporary workaround and comparison, not a proven root-cause diagnosis.

solution.intent: Try a newer maintenance release rather than remaining on the downgraded version, then observe whether Zigbee responsiveness remains normal.
solution.concrete_example: Install the next available Core maintenance release and retest the same Zigbee light commands.

edges.comment: Reporter c14: after installing 2022.9.2, the original reporter initially believed the problem was fixed but deliberately waited for further observations.

solution.intent: Update to a later patch release in the expectation that the initially observed recovery will persist.
solution.concrete_example: Install the later patch release and continue monitoring the same Zigbee network.

edges.comment: Reporter c17 and c19: the original reporter closed after apparent recovery, then reopened because the behavior was intermittent and returned on 2022.9.4. The later patch update did not provide a durable resolution.

question_patterns: How is the Zigbee coordinator connected, and is it close to a Wi-Fi access point or other radio equipment?
Is the Zigbee stick connected through an extension cable and physically separated from access points?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My zzh stick is directly connected to my NUC through a two-foot USB extension cable, and it is not near any access points.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Zigbee stick is plugged directly into a USB 3 port beside my Wi-Fi access point and Bluetooth adapter, with no extension cable.
The extension cable is three feet instead of two, and the stick is still away from the access point.

question_patterns: Is a Bluetooth adapter connected to the same host, and where is it positioned relative to the Zigbee stick?
Do you have Bluetooth hardware connected near the coordinator?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have a Bluetooth adapter plugged into a USB hub on a two-foot cable from another USB port.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no Bluetooth hardware enabled or connected to this host.

question_patterns: What hardware is Home Assistant running on, and are the USB ports USB 3?
Are any USB 3 devices or ports involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Home Assistant is running on a NUC, and all of its USB ports are USB 3.0.

question_patterns: Can you enable ZHA debug logging and capture the complete log while the delay is occurring?
What errors appear in the ZHA debug log during an unresponsive period?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: While the lights were unresponsive, the log repeatedly printed "AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'request_callback_rsp'" from zigpy_znp while ZHA was trying to read light state.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The ZHA debug log remains clean during the delay, with successful transmissions and acknowledgements for every command.
The same exception appears fewer times during a shorter capture.

edges.comment: Original reporter c20-c21 and c38-c45: the maintainer requested topology details and debug logging. The original reporter supplied the NUC/USB layout and raw exception, then volunteered the key directional observation that inbound sensor events remain immediate while commands to lights are delayed. The maintainer interpreted the exception as a ZHA-to-radio connection breakdown; that interpretation is not placed in the user's answer.

solution.intent: Disable Bluetooth to reduce possible 2.4 GHz RF interference that may be preventing the Zigbee coordinator from transmitting.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily disable Bluetooth on the host, restart if required, and compare outbound Zigbee command latency.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer inferred from successful inbound traffic and failed or delayed outbound traffic that the radio might perceive excessive RF noise and refuse to transmit. The thread never establishes that Bluetooth interference is the definitive root cause.

edges.comment: Participant2 c52 suggested disabling Bluetooth on participant10's Raspberry Pi/RaspBee deployment. Participant10 c55 reported improvement but not restoration to prior performance, while participant9 c56 said Bluetooth was already disabled despite continued lag. These are different affected deployments folded into the simulated user side; they are not the original reporter's NUC configuration. The workaround is therefore a real but incomplete/falsified resolution.

solution.intent: Update Home Assistant Core to the current maintenance release reported to restore normal Zigbee responsiveness, but do not claim a confirmed mechanism and ask the original reporter to verify on their own system.
solution.concrete_example: Update to the current Core maintenance release, retest both outbound light commands and inbound sensor events, and report whether the long delays recur. Other affected users later reported normal operation, but the thread does not identify which change corrected it.

edges.comment: Participants9 and 10 c57-c58, on their own affected Raspberry Pi/RaspBee deployments, reported that updating to 2022.10.2 removed the delays. Neither knew which change fixed the behavior. The original reporter never confirmed that release on the NUC/zzh setup, so the terminal remains unverified and user_perceives_resolved is false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the established failure pattern rather than inventing a definitive code-level root cause: inbound Zigbee sensor events remain immediate while outbound commands can be delayed for minutes, alongside zigpy-znp connection or callback errors.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the version comparisons, directional traffic observation, USB/radio layout, and debug-log exception.

Must not claim Bluetooth interference is the confirmed root cause or disabling Bluetooth is the complete fix; it only partially improved one affected deployment and another affected deployment already had Bluetooth disabled.

Must recommend updating to the current maintenance release reported by other affected users to restore responsiveness, while stating that the thread does not establish which underlying change fixed it.
Must ask the original reporter to verify both outbound commands and inbound events on their own system before declaring the issue resolved.
Must not merge the unrelated gateway-pairing screenshots or the separate participant's coordinator-reflashing problem into the original reporter's diagnostic chain.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Home Assistant user who can downgrade and update Core, inspect logs, describe USB and radio placement, and compare entity behavior, but does not perform source-level debugging.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and persistent; provides practical observations, challenges explanations that conflict with observed behavior, and adds concise follow-up details as the intermittent issue recurs.
